sanskrit: atīmām akhyaṃ pṛthivīm ati dyām ati sūryam | ati viśvam idaṃ bhūtam aty akhyaṃ yātudhānyaḥ ||
english: I have seen beyond this earth, beyond the sky, beyond the sun; beyond all these beings I have seen — the demonesses have been seen through.

sanskrit: darśaya mā yātudhānān darśaya yātudhānyaḥ | aghāyūn sarvān darśaya- -iti tvauṣadha ā rabhe ||
english: Show me the sorcerers, show me the demonesses; show me all those who intend evil — with this in mind I take hold of you, O herb.

sanskrit: evā sahasracakṣo tvaṃ prati paśyāsy āyataḥ | saho 'si yātudhānajambhanam ||
english: Thus you, thousand-eyed one, see forward as you approach; you are the power that devours the sorcerers.

sanskrit: imāḥ pāre pṛdākvas triṣaptā nirjarāyavaḥ | tāsāṃ jarāyuṇā vayam akṣyāv api vyayāmasy aghāyoḥ paripanthinaḥ ||
english: These serpent-like creatures here on the far side, three times seven, shedding their skins — with their shed skin we cover the eyes of the one who lies in wait with evil intent.

sanskrit: viṣūcy etu kṛntatī pinākam iva bibhratī | viṣvak punarbhuvā mano 'samṛddhā aghāyavaḥ ||
english: Let her go in all directions, cutting, bearing a club as it were; those with evil intent who reappear repeatedly in every direction — may they be unfulfilled.

sanskrit: apetaḥ paripanthino +'po aghāyur arṣatu | na bahavaḥ saṃ śaknavan nārbhakā abhi dhṛṣṇavan ||
english: Away, you lurkers on the path! Let the evildoer flow away like water. Let neither the many be able to overpower, nor the small ones dare to attack.

sanskrit: pretaṃ pādau pra sphurataṃ vahataṃ pṛṇato gṛham | indrāṇy etu prathamā- -ajītāmuṣitā pathā ||
english: Go forward, kick with both feet, carry to the house of the generous giver; let Indrāṇī go first — unconquered, unrobbed, along the path.

sanskrit: āyam agan phālgumaṇir balena baladāḥ saha | yenendro dasyūnāṃ vīrām̐ asurāṇām avātirat ||
english: The Phālguna gem has come here, together with strength and the bestower of strength — that by which Indra cut down the heroes of the Dasyus and the Asuras.

sanskrit: varcasā māṃ payasokṣantu devā varcasā dyāvāpṛthivī ubhe | varco me devaḥ savitā dadhātu varco vipraḥ kaśyapo me dadhātu ||
english: May the gods anoint me with radiance and milk; may both heaven and earth anoint me with radiance; may god Savitā bestow radiance upon me, may the wise sage Kaśyapa bestow radiance upon me.

sanskrit: varco ma āpo dadhatu varco me vīrudho dadhan | bhūtāni sarvāḥ saṅgatya varca ā dhur mukhe mama ||
english: May the waters bestow radiance upon me, may the plants bestow radiance upon me; let all beings, coming together, place radiance in my face.

sanskrit: yāḥ purastād vitiṣṭhante gāvaḥ pravrājinīr iva | vātīkṛtasya bheṣajīḥ pippalīḥ pārayiṣṇavaḥ ||
english: Those that stand spread out in the east, like cows wandering on the road — the long-pepper plants, healers of wind-sickness, carrying one across.

sanskrit: rudrasya mūtram asy amṛtasya nābhiḥ | pṛthivyāṃ mūlaṃ niṣṭhitam asi viṣāṇā nāma vātīkṛtabheṣajī ||
english: You are the urine of Rudra, the navel of the immortal; you are established as a root in the earth — named Viṣāṇā, healer of wind-sickness.

sanskrit: śaṃ te astu matasnābhyāṃ śaṃ yakne śaṃ talīdyai | śaṃ te pṛṣṭibhyo majjabhyaḥ śam astu tanve tava ||
english: May there be well-being for your kidneys, well-being for your liver, well-being for your spleen; may there be well-being for your ribs and marrow, may there be well-being for your body.

sanskrit: na hi te agne tanvaḥ krūram ānaṃśa martyam | kapir babhastu tejanaṃ svaṃ jarāyu gaur iva ||
english: For the cruel thing has not reached your body, O Agni, the mortal; let the monkey, the brown one, sharpen its own point — like a cow its calf-membrane.

sanskrit: tveṣa iva saṃ ca vi ca roruvaṇyate yad uttaradrā uparasya khādati | śīrṣṇā śiro apsasāpso ardayann aṃśūn babhastu haritebhir āśubhiḥ ||
english: It roars together and apart like a storm, when the upper one gnaws the lower; crushing head with head, water with water, the brown one with the swift green ones flays the shoots.

sanskrit: suparṇā vācam akratopa dyavy ākhare kṛṣṇā iṣirā anartiṣuḥ | ni yan niyanty uparasya niṣkṛtiṃ purū reto dadhire sūryasyutaḥ ||
english: The birds of good feather raised their voice upon the heavenly perch; the black, vigorous ones danced; when they lead down the expiation of the lower one, the many have placed their seed — sped by the sun.

sanskrit: bhagena mā śāṃśapena sākam indreṇa medinā | kṛṇomi bhaginaṃ mā- -apa drāntv arātayaḥ ||
english: With the Śāṃśapa-bhaga, together with the ally Indra, I make myself prosperous — let all enmities flee away.

sanskrit: yo andho yaḥ punaḥsaro bhago vṛkṣeṣv ārpitaḥ | bhago me astu śāṃśapo 'pa drāntv arātayaḥ ||
english: The one that is blind, the one that flows again — the bhaga established in the trees; may the Śāṃśapa-bhaga be mine — let all enmities flee away.

sanskrit: yathā vṛkṣām̐ abhyabhavaḥ sākam indreṇa medinā | evā mā bhaginaṃ kṛṇv apa drāntv arātayaḥ ||
english: As you overcame the trees together with the ally Indra, so make me prosperous — let all enmities flee away.

sanskrit: apeto nīlalohitaṃ jātaṃ himavatas pari | kīśmīlam urvarābhyo divo jātam anīnaśam ||
english: The blue-red one, born from around the Himālayas — the Kīśmīla demon born from the sky upon the plowed fields — I have driven it away.

sanskrit: abhrāj jātaṃ varṣāj jātam atho jātaṃ divas pari | atho samudrād jātaṃ kīśmīlaṃ nāśayāmasi ||
english: Born from a cloud, born from the rain, born from around the sky, born from the ocean — the Kīśmīla we destroy.

sanskrit: yo nīhārād yaḥ pruṣvā yo adbhyas pari jāyase | garbho yo vidyutām asi sa naḥ kīśmīla mṛḍaya ||
english: You who are born from fog, you who are born from dew, you who are born from water — you who are the embryo of lightning, O Kīśmīla, be gracious to us.

sanskrit: nodeyīḥ sikatā imāḥ sindhutas paryābhṛtāḥ | tābhir yamasya kīśmīlaṃ saṃbhṛtābhir anīnaśam ||
english: These sand grains, brought from around the river, which cannot be counted — with those gathered grains I have driven away Yama's Kīśmīla.

sanskrit: tvayā pūrvaṃ vibhīdaka saṃjitā asurā hatāḥ | tvaṃ sapatnacātano bhrātṛvyām̐ ava dhūnuṣva ||
english: By you, O Vibhīdaka tree, the Asuras were formerly defeated and slain; you who drive away rivals — shake off the enemies.

sanskrit: vi bhinattu vibhīdakas tīkṣṇaśṛṅga iva ṛṣabhaḥ | atho sapatnān ā dattām atho hantu durasyataḥ ||
english: Let the Vibhīdaka split them apart like a bull with sharp horns; and may it subdue the rivals, and may it strike down those who show malice.

sanskrit: vyavadhīt sahamānaḥ sapatnān dviṣato me 'dharām̐ akaḥ | abhy abhūd bhūtyobhayām ||
english: The overpowering one has cut through the rivals, has laid low those who hate me; it has prevailed over them, possessing prosperity on both sides.

sanskrit: ya āskandaḥ parāskanda ākhuḥ kakubha āt krimiḥ | upajīkām̐ upakvasān tān sarvān jambhayāmasi ||
english: The attacker, the counter-attacker, the mouse, the Kakubha-worm, the earthworm — the small creatures, the chirping ones — all of these we crush.

sanskrit: api nahyāmy ākhor muñjena mukham āsyam | anadaṃ yathā carād apaitum urvarābhyaḥ ||
english: I bind shut the face, the mouth, of the mouse with Muñja grass — so that, unable to eat, it may go away from the plowed fields.

sanskrit: apinahyamukha ākhuḥ paroktaḥ prāṭparāṇutaḥ | śṛṇāmy asya dantān nir akṣau pādayāmasi ||
english: The mouse with bound mouth, thrust away, driven far off and repelled — I break its teeth; we knock out its two eyes.

sanskrit: aśvinā sāraghena mā madhunāṅkta śubhaspatī | yathā varcasvatīṃ vācam āvadāni janām̐ anu ||
english: O Aśvins, lords of the auspicious, anoint me with the honey of the bee, so that I may speak a speech full of radiance among the people.

sanskrit: yaśā ahaṃ nimiṣate pratikhyātre yaśā aham | atraimi tad yaśā aham uta tatra yaśā aham ||
english: I am glorious to the one who blinks, I am glorious to the one who beholds in return; I come here as glorious, and I am glorious there too.

sanskrit: asmai ca sarvasmai bhūtāya sarvasmai ca vipaśyate | sarvasmā id ahaṃ yaśāḥ ||
english: To every being here, and to every one who sees — to all of them I am indeed glorious.

sanskrit: apottudāporṇuhi yadīdam asti vā na vā | vyandhyaṃ vyalguṇaṃ cakṣur akṣībhyāṃ kṛdhi ||
english: Push away, uncover whatever this is or is not; make the sight blind and impaired — do this to the eyes.

sanskrit: aṅgaṃ hiraṇyayaṃ kṛtvā laṅgalāṣam armaṃ ca | tad devā apa lumpata ||
english: Having made the golden limb, the plow-handle, and the cataract — gods, take that away.

sanskrit: cakṣuṣman me mano astu cakṣuṣmad dhṛdayaṃ mama | cakṣuṣmac cittam astu me cakṣuś cakṣuṣmad astu me cakṣur ā dhehi me 'kṣyoḥ ||
english: May my mind be possessed of sight, may my heart be possessed of sight; may my consciousness be possessed of sight, may my eye be possessed of sight — place sight in my two eyes.

sanskrit: somo rājā savitā ca rājā bhavo rājā bhuvanaṃ ca rājā | śarvo rājā śarma ca rājā ta u naḥ śarma yacchantu devāḥ ||
english: Soma is king, and Savitā is king, Bhava is king, and the world is king; Śarva is king and Śarman is king — may those gods grant us shelter.

sanskrit: ādityair no bṛhaspatir bhagaḥ somena naḥ saha | viśve devā urv antarikṣaṃ ta u naḥ śarma yacchantu devāḥ ||
english: Bṛhaspati with the Ādityas, Bhaga together with Soma, the All-Gods, the wide atmosphere — may those gods grant us shelter.

sanskrit: utāviddhāṃ niṣkhidata- -atho śrathnīthāyatām | mā no viśve devā maruto hetim asthata ||
english: Strike out the un-pierced one and also loosen the taut one; O All-Gods, O Maruts, do not direct your missile at us.

sanskrit: apām idaṃ nyayanaṃ samudrasya niveśanam | madhye hradasya no gṛhāḥ parācīnā mukhā kṛdhi ||
english: This is the flowing-down of waters, the resting place of the ocean; make our houses face away in the middle of the lake.

sanskrit: āyane te parāyaṇe dūrvā rohatu puṣpiṇī | utso vātra jāyatāṃ hrado vā puṇḍarīkavān ||
english: On your coming and on your going, may blossoming Dūrvā grass grow; or may a spring arise here, or a lotus-filled lake.

sanskrit: himasya tvā jarāyuṇā śāle pari vyayāmasi | śītahradāya no bhuvo 'gnir dadātu bheṣajam ||
english: With the after-birth of snow, O house, we wrap you around; may you be for us a cool lake, may Agni grant the remedy.

sanskrit: ayaṃ darbho vimanyukaḥ svāya cāraṇāya ca | manyor vimanyuko manyuśamano astu te ||
english: This Darbha grass is free of anger, for one's own sake and for wandering; freed of anger it is the calmer of anger — may it be that for you.

sanskrit: ayaṃ yo bhūrimūlaḥ samudram avagacchati | darbhaḥ pṛthivyāṃ niṣṭhitaḥ sa te astu vimanyukaḥ ||
english: This one with many roots goes down to the ocean; the Darbha grass established in the earth — may that be free of anger for you.

sanskrit: vi te hanavyāṃ śaraṇiṃ vi te mukhyāṃ nayāmasi | yathāvaśo na vādiṣo mama cittam upāsāsai ||
english: We lead away the path of your jaw, the path of your mouth; so that, being under my control and without protest, you may sit up near my mind.

sanskrit: yebhiḥ pāśaiḥ parivitto vibaddhaḥ parauparāv ārpito aṅgeaṅge | vi te cṛtyantāṃ vicṛto hi santi bhrūṇaghni pūsan duritāni mṛṣṭām ||
english: With whatever bonds you are wrapped round and bound, fixed limb upon limb again and again — may they be unraveled for you, for the cut ones exist as cut; O Pūṣan, wiper-away, may he wipe away the sins of the embryo-slayer.

sanskrit: trite devā amṛjataina etat trita enan manuṣyeṣv amṛṣṭa | tato yadi tvā madhye na ārat tad ahaṃ tvad brahmaṇāpā karomi ||
english: The gods wiped this off upon Trita; Trita wiped it off upon human beings; if it has not gotten away from you at the middle then I remove it from you by the sacred formula.

sanskrit: marīcīr dhūmaṃ pra viśānu vātam udārān gacchota vā nīhāram | nadīnāṃ phenam anu tad vi naśyatu bhrūṇaghni pūṣan duritāni mṛṣṭām ||
english: Enter the heat rays, enter the smoke along the wind, go to the lofty ones, or else to the mist; following the foam of rivers may that vanish away — O Pūṣan, wiper-away, may he wipe away the sins of the embryo-slayer.

sanskrit: agne rakṣaḥ prati daha yat kumbhyābhir ābhṛtam | anādhṛṣyaḥ sa yāsyaty abhūj jīvātave ayam ||
english: O Agni, burn back the demon-brought thing that has been brought in pots; that one will go away unapproachable — this one has become able to live.

sanskrit: yan nakhavad yac chaphavat prasūmat kiṃ ca puṣpavat | urvā matsyo madhūlakaṃ tasya pāsyaty ayam anāsrāvam arogaṇam ||
english: Whatever is claw-like, whatever is hoof-like, whatever sprouts, whatever is flower-like — the Urvā fish, the Madhūlaka plant: this one will drink of that, free of flux, free of disease.

sanskrit: yāḥ samudrāt prasravanti devīr himavatas pari | āpo yā viśvaśambhuvas tā ihā yantu bheṣajīḥ ||
english: The divine waters that flow from the ocean and from around the Himālayas — the waters that bring well-being to all — may those healing ones come here.
